claims.text: The subconscious mind controls most critical survival behaviors instinctively and unconsciously—such as avoiding cliffs and jumping out of the way of buses—rather than through conscious control. Conscious reason cannot will autonomic functions like heartbeat acceleration or pupil dilation.
claims.speaker: Unknown
claims.mechanism: Autonomic nervous system operates independently of conscious override; instinctive survival responses evolved before conscious reasoning capacity.
bounded_by: Conscious mind can nudge or redirect unconscious impulses but cannot override fundamental instincts
Does not apply to learned behaviors acquired through conscious training

claims.text: Rory Sutherland describes a counterintuitive test result for manufacturer websites: making the button routing buyers to a third-party retailer (Amazon, John Lewis) green and the manufacturer's own direct-purchase button grey -- routing buyers toward the lower-margin channel -- can in some cases result in higher total revenue overall, because it coheres with customers' instinctive preference for third-party purchase environments.
claims.speaker: Rory Sutherland
conditions: e-commerce manufacturer websites
product categories where consumers instinctively prefer buying from trusted third-party retailers over manufacturer direct
claims.mechanism: When the design of choices coheres with instinctive consumer urges, a far higher proportion of visitors click through to buy; the volume uplift on the intermediary channel can exceed the per-unit margin loss, yielding higher total revenue even though the proportion of direct sales falls.
bounded_by: Does not apply universally; depends on the gap between consumer instinct and channel margin; must be tested per product category

claims.text: Ruth Snowden-Gough (CMO, Hain Celestial UK) asserts that continuous free trial via sampling is a necessary demand-generation tactic in stigmatized food categories because trial is the primary mechanism for overcoming category preconceptions that cannot be resolved through advertising alone.
claims.speaker: Ruth Snowden-Gough
conditions: FMCG categories with historical negative perception (frozen food, plant-based meat, low-alcohol)
products where taste is the primary adoption barrier
claims.mechanism: Consumers hold category preconceptions formed by previous (worse) product experiences; advertising cannot override a sensory memory. Direct trial resets the sensory reference and removes the prior negative anchor.
bounded_by: Does not apply when the adoption barrier is price or distribution, not taste perception

conditions: Business operating at national or international scale
Comparison is over a 12-month measurement window for brand vs. 30-day window for direct response

attribution measured over 6-12 month horizon vs. 30-60 day horizon
brand at revenue plateau caused by margin compression from performance-only spend
marketing investment decisions over multi-year horizons
marketing organizations measuring effectiveness through last-click or short-window attribution models

claims.text: Alex Hormozi recounts that when he responded to a competitor threat at Gym Launch by cutting his recurring product price (reducing top-line by roughly $500,000 per month) while adding more value, his churn rate did not change — meaning the revenue reduction was entirely unrecoverable loss with no retention benefit.

price reduction made in response to a competitor entering with lower pricing

claims.text: Alex Hormozi argues that the binding constraint preventing most small-to-mid-market founders from attracting world-class talent is not compensation level but the credibility of the vision; world-class talent evaluates the size of the opportunity and the founder's demonstrated character before accepting an offer, making vision scale and founder reputation the primary hiring levers.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.speaker_term: they don't want to work for you
conditions: Has not achieved an exit or large brand sufficient to attract top talent by reputation alone
Recruiting executives who have non-financial alternatives
Small business founder
Small businesses where founders have not yet achieved significant scale or notoriety
founder trying to hire above current company size
sub-$50M revenue businesses
claims.mechanism: World-class talent at the $500K+ level has abundant options; they evaluate whether the founder's vision is large enough to accommodate their own aspirations and whether the founder's character (consistency, no emotional volatility) makes them a safe bet to follow; insufficient vision or character credibility is the bottleneck, not compensation budget.
bounded_by: At $100M+ revenue, compensation and enterprise validation can substitute for some vision credibility
Does not apply in specialized technical roles where skill scarcity makes candidates less selective about vision
Does not apply to founders who have achieved large-scale exits or have a recognized brand (e.g., Steve Jobs, Richard Branson) where world-class talent actively seeks them out

claims.text: Alex Hormozi argues that when a B2B service business has a low close rate, the true problem is almost always upstream of the sales call — in avatar clarity, offer structure, positioning, or messaging — not in the close mechanics themselves.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: B2B service business
founder attributes close-rate problem to sales technique
claims.mechanism: Weak upstream inputs (vague avatar, unstructured offer, poor positioning) mean the wrong prospects reach the sales call, making close rate a symptom rather than the root cause.
